hook.text: Fuel cells need platinum catalysts costing thousands per gram — nano engineering slashes usage by 90%.

buildup.text: Nanoparticles expose more platinum atoms on the surface — fewer grams deliver the same catalytic activity.

discovery.text: Core-shell nanoparticles put platinum only on the surface — cheap metal cores underneath carry the structure.

twist.text: Platinum nanoparticles dissolve slowly in acidic fuel cell conditions — degradation reduces lifetime and performance.

climax.text: Single-atom catalysts anchor individual platinum atoms on carbon supports — ultimate atom efficiency, zero waste.

punchline.text: Use every platinum atom — nano catalysis makes fuel cells affordable.

quiz.question: How do core-shell nanoparticles reduce platinum use in fuel cells?
options: They replace platinum with iron entirely
Platinum is placed only on the particle surface over a cheaper metal core, maximizing atom efficiency
They increase the fuel cell's operating temperature to need less catalyst
